prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s manifesto is a plan to end 14 years of Conservative chaos, restore hope, and rebuild a Britain that serves working people. It promises mission-driven government, built on national security, secure borders and economic stability, partnering with business and unions, and underpinned by rock-solid fiscal rules.

First steps for change
- Economic stability with tough spending rules to keep taxes, inflation and mortgages as low as possible.
- Cut NHS waiting lists with 40,000 extra weekly appointments, funded by a crackdown on tax avoidance and ending non-dom status.
- A new Border Security Command using counter-terror powers to smash smuggler gangs.
- Great British Energy, a publicly owned clean power company, funded by a strengthened windfall tax.
- Crack down on antisocial behaviour with more neighbourhood police and youth hubs.
- Recruit 6,500 teachers in key subjects, funded by ending private school tax breaks.

Strong foundations
- National security: unshakeable NATO commitment, the UK’s nuclear deterrent retained, a Strategic Defence Review and a path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; Martyn’s Law; updated counter-extremism powers.
- Secure borders: scrap Rwanda, clear the asylum backlog, end hotel use, fast-track returns, and a new EU security agreement.
- Economic stability: current budget balance and falling debt; OBR oversight of every fiscal event; recoup Covid fraud; no rises to NI, Income Tax rates or VAT; abolish non-dom status; close tax loopholes; modernise HMRC.

Five missions and core policies
- Kickstart growth: a pro-business, pro-worker industrial strategy; a National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to unlock private investment in ports, gigafactories, steel, CCS and green hydrogen; cap corporation tax at 25%, permanent full expensing; replace business rates; 10-year infrastructure plan; rail brought into public ownership as contracts expire; EV rollout, roads maintained and 1m potholes fixed annually; full gigabit and national 5G by 2030; 1.5m homes with planning reform, new towns, more social homes; devolution and Local Growth Plans; a New Deal for Working People (ban exploitative zero-hours, end fire-and-rehire, day-one rights, a genuine living wage for all adults).
- Clean energy superpower: zero-carbon electricity by 2030 with doubled onshore wind, tripled solar, quadrupled offshore wind; invest in nuclear and storage; no new North Sea exploration licences but manage existing fields; Great British Energy (£8.3bn, HQ in Scotland); Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes; clean up rivers with tougher water regulation; support farmers and boost nature.
- Take back our streets: restore neighbourhood policing; Respect Orders for persistent offenders; protect shopworkers; halve knife crime with bans, tough consequences and Young Futures hubs; specialist rape units and courts; raise policing standards; expand fraud strategy; fix prisons and cut reoffending.
- Break down barriers to opportunity: 3,000 school-based nurseries; free breakfast clubs in every primary; 6,500 new teachers; curriculum and assessment reform; mental health support in all schools; Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; a flexible Growth and Skills Levy; protect and improve HE; expand access to arts, sport and culture; robust equality agenda including a Race Equality Act, disability and ethnicity pay gap reporting, and a full ban on conversion practices.
- Build an NHS fit for the future: 2m extra operations/scans/appointments a year; double CT/MRI scanners; deliver the New Hospitals Programme; transform the NHS app; restore the family doctor; pharmacy prescribing; a Dentistry Rescue Plan; a National Care Service with a Fair Pay Agreement; 8,500 more mental health staff; strong public health action on smoking, youth vaping and junk food ads.

Clean politics and a reconnected Britain
- An independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; modernise the Commons; immediate Lords reform (end hereditary peers; retirement at 80) and consult on full replacement; votes at 16; reset relations with devolved governments.
- Stand firm with NATO and Ukraine; AUKUS; a clear-eyed China policy; make Brexit work with better EU trade and a security pact (no return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement); targeted trade deals; global climate leadership with a Clean Power Alliance; modernise international development and restore 0.7% when fiscal conditions allow.

Fully costed and fiscally responsible, Labour’s plan will stop the chaos, turn the page, and start national renewal in the service of working people.
